answers.question: Do AI images my app generates for EU users have to be marked?
answers.description: Yes: since 2 August 2026 under EU AI Act Article 50(2), whoever's model makes them. What the rule says, what the Code expects, and the sources.
answers.answer: Yes. If your product lets people generate images under your name for users in the EU, you are the provider, whoever's model makes the image, and since 2 August 2026 every output has to be marked in a machine-readable, detectable way.

findings.title: Mark every output in a machine-readable, detectable way
findings.summary: If you offer generation to users in the EU under your own name, you are the provider, whoever's model produces the output, and every image, video, audio or text output must be marked so that machines can detect it as AI-generated. The Act names no technology; the Code of Practice says what counts as adequate. Standard editing assistance is excluded.
findings.quote: outputs ... are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated

answers.question: Do I have to label realistic AI images and videos I publish in the EU?
answers.description: Yes: Article 50(4) of the EU AI Act requires disclosure of deepfakes, realistic AI content of people, places or events. The rule and sources.
answers.answer: Yes. If you publish AI-generated or manipulated images or video that realistically show people, places or events, Article 50(4) requires you to disclose that they are artificial, clearly and at the latest when people first see them.

findings.title: Disclose realistic AI images, video and audio you publish
findings.summary: If you publish AI-generated or manipulated images, video or audio that realistically show people, places or events (deepfakes), you must disclose that they are artificially generated or manipulated, clearly and at the latest when people first see them. This checker does not assess the Act's exceptions; the law page sets out the article.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the AI Act), Articles 50, 99 and 113, Official Journal text

answers.question: Do AI-written articles need an AI label in the EU?
answers.description: AI text published to inform the public on matters of public interest must be disclosed under EU AI Act Article 50(4), unless a person edits it.
answers.answer: Yes, if they inform the public on matters of public interest and no person has taken editorial responsibility for them: Article 50(4) requires such AI-generated text to be disclosed as AI-generated.

findings.title: Disclose AI text published on matters of public interest
findings.summary: AI-generated text published to inform the public on matters of public interest must be disclosed as AI-generated, unless a person has taken editorial responsibility for it.

answers.question: Does California's AI Transparency Act apply to my AI image generator?
answers.description: If it has over 1,000,000 monthly users and is publicly accessible in California: latent disclosure, a visible option and a free detection tool.
answers.answer: Yes, if your generator has more than 1,000,000 monthly users and is publicly accessible in California. Since 2 August 2026 every AI image, video and audio output needs a latent disclosure, users must be offered a visible one, and you must run a free public detection tool with an API.

findings.title: A free public detection tool with an API
findings.summary: Run a free, publicly accessible tool that checks uploads or URLs for your system's provenance data, with an API so it can be used without visiting your site, and that collects no personal information beyond optional feedback contact details.
findings.quote: at no cost to the user

sources.title: California Business and Professions Code, sections 22757.1 to 22757.6 (FindLaw's copy, current as of 1 January 2026)

findings.title: A latent disclosure in every image, video and audio output
findings.summary: If your generative system has over 1,000,000 monthly users and is publicly accessible in California, embed a latent disclosure in every AI-generated image, video and audio file: where feasible, your name, the system's name and version, the time and date, and a unique identifier. It must be detectable by your own detection tool, follow widely accepted industry standards, and be extraordinarily difficult to remove. Text is not covered.
findings.quote: This chapter shall become operative on August 2, 2026.

sources.title: California Business and Professions Code, sections 22757.1 to 22757.6 (FindLaw's copy, current as of 1 January 2026)
AB 853 (2025), Chapter 674, Statutes of 2025: bill page and digest

findings.title: Offer users a visible disclosure
findings.summary: Offer your users the option to include a visible disclosure that identifies the content as AI-generated, appropriate to the medium and as hard to remove as is technically feasible.
findings.quote: clear, conspicuous, appropriate for the medium of the content

sources.title: California Business and Professions Code, sections 22757.1 to 22757.6 (FindLaw's copy, current as of 1 January 2026)

answers.question: Does California's AI law apply to a small AI app?
answers.description: Not directly: the AI Transparency Act binds generative AI providers with over 1,000,000 monthly users. What applies below that, with sources.
answers.answer: Not directly. California's AI Transparency Act binds providers whose system has more than 1,000,000 monthly users; below that its disclosure and detection duties do not apply to you, though the platforms and hosts you use take on their own duties from 2027.

answers.question: What labels does China require on AI-generated content?
answers.description: Two since 1 September 2025: a visible label and the AIGC metadata field of GB 45438-2025, which a C2PA manifest does not replace. Rules and sources.
answers.answer: Two, since 1 September 2025, if your service is offered to users in mainland China: a visible label a person can see or hear, and an implicit label in the file's metadata, the AIGC field fixed by GB 45438-2025. A C2PA manifest does not replace that field. Your user agreement must explain the labels, and removing labels, or supplying tools to, is prohibited.

findings.title: The AIGC metadata field in every file
findings.summary: Write an implicit label into the file's metadata: a field named AIGC with seven keys (the label value, your name or code as producer, your content number, and the reserved and distributor keys), as Annex E of GB 45438-2025 fixes. A C2PA manifest does not replace it, and it must be written before any manifest is signed. Watermarks are encouraged, not required.
findings.quote: production element information such as the attribute of the generated content, the service provider's name or code, and a content number
findings.unverified: Where the field goes in each file format is in TC260 practice guides we have not read. That the Measures reach only services offered to the public in mainland China is from memory.

sources.title: Measures for the Labelling of AI-Generated and Synthetic Content (人工智能生成合成内容标识办法), notice of 7 March 2025, published by the Cyberspace Administration of China on 14 March 2025; Chinese text, our translation
GB 45438-2025, Cybersecurity technology: labelling method for content generated by artificial intelligence (in force 1 September 2025), full Chinese text as hosted by Sidley; our translation

findings.title: A visible label on generated content
findings.summary: If your generation service is offered to users in mainland China, generated text, images, audio and video carry an explicit label a person can see or hear, containing "AI" (or 人工智能) and "generated" (生成) or "synthesised" (合成). On images and video it is text at an edge or corner at least 5% of the shortest side high; audio gets a spoken notice or the Morse rhythm for "AI". Exported files keep the label unless the user asks otherwise under your agreement, and then you keep logs for six months.
findings.quote: ensure the file contains an explicit label that meets the requirements
findings.unverified: Which services must add the visible label is set by Article 17(1) of the deep synthesis provisions, which we have not re-read; the standard's Annex B lists text-to-image, music and video, cloned voices and face generation as typical. That the Measures reach only services offered to the public in mainland China is from memory.

GB 45438-2025, Cybersecurity technology: labelling method for content generated by artificial intelligence (in force 1 September 2025), full Chinese text as hosted by Sidley; our translation

findings.title: Do not remove or hide labels, or help others to
findings.summary: Deleting, altering, forging or hiding an AI label is prohibited, and so is supplying tools to do it.

findings.title: Explain the labels in your user agreement
findings.summary: Your user agreement states how and in what style content is labelled, and prompts users to read the labelling requirements.

answers.question: What does South Korea's AI Basic Act require of generative AI services?
answers.description: Since 22 January 2026: tell users in advance that the service runs on AI, and label output visibly or machine-readably. Article 31 with sources.
answers.answer: If Korean users can reach your product, since 22 January 2026 you must tell them in advance that it runs on generative AI, and label its output as AI-generated, either visibly or machine-readably; a machine-readable label needs a one-time notice to the user as well. The Act reaches businesses abroad.

findings.title: Tell users in advance that the service runs on AI
findings.summary: If Korean users can reach your generative AI product, tell them in advance that it runs on generative AI: in the terms, contract or manual, on the screen, or where the service is provided. This is the Article 31 duty with a direct fine of up to KRW 30 million. The Act applies to businesses abroad whose service affects Korean users.

sources.title: Framework Act on the Development of Artificial Intelligence and the Establishment of a Foundation for Trust (인공지능 발전과 신뢰 기반 조성 등에 관한 기본법), consolidated text; Korean text, our translation
Enforcement Decree of the same Act, consolidated text in force 20 August 2026; Korean text, our translation

findings.title: Label generated output, visibly or machine-readably
findings.summary: Indicate that output was generated by generative AI, either in a way a person can perceive or in a way a machine can read; if you choose machine-readable (a signed manifest or a watermark), also tell the user at least once, in text or voice, that the output is AI-generated. Not needed where AI use is obvious from the product or the output.

answers.question: Does realistic AI video need a visible label in South Korea?
answers.description: Yes: under Article 31(3) of the AI Basic Act, output hard to tell from reality must be labelled so users clearly recognise it. The rule and sources.
answers.answer: Yes. Where your system produces sound, images or video that are hard to tell from reality, Article 31(3) requires a notice or label the user can clearly recognise, on top of the prior notice and the output label every generative service owes Korean users.

findings.title: Tell users in advance that the service runs on AI
findings.summary: If Korean users can reach your generative AI product, tell them in advance that it runs on generative AI: in the terms, contract or manual, on the screen, or where the service is provided. This is the Article 31 duty with a direct fine of up to KRW 30 million. The Act applies to businesses abroad whose service affects Korean users.

Enforcement Decree of the same Act, consolidated text in force 20 August 2026; Korean text, our translation

findings.title: Label generated output, visibly or machine-readably
findings.summary: Indicate that output was generated by generative AI, either in a way a person can perceive or in a way a machine can read; if you choose machine-readable (a signed manifest or a watermark), also tell the user at least once, in text or voice, that the output is AI-generated. Not needed where AI use is obvious from the product or the output.
findings.quote: a method a machine can read

findings.title: A clear label on output that could pass as real
findings.summary: Where your system produces sound, images or video that are hard to tell from reality, notify or label it so the user can clearly recognise it as generated. Artistic and creative works may be labelled in a way that does not spoil them.
findings.quote: in a manner the user can clearly recognise

answers.question: Do realistic AI images need a label in India?
answers.description: Yes, since 20 February 2026: a prominent label, permanent metadata with a unique identifier, and no way to remove either. India's IT Rules with sources.
answers.answer: Yes. Since 20 February 2026 a service that can create realistic AI audio, images or video of people or events must label the output prominently, embed permanent metadata with a unique identifier for the service, let no one remove either, block unlawful synthetic content and remind users of the rules every three months.

findings.title: No way to remove the label or metadata
findings.summary: Your service must not let users modify, suppress or remove the label or the metadata, including the unique identifier.
findings.quote: the intermediary shall not enable the modification, suppression or removal of the label, permanent metadata, including the unique identifier

sources.title: Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Amendment Rules, 2026, notification G.S.R. 120(E) of 10 February 2026, Gazette of India, as published by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology

findings.title: Permanent metadata with a unique identifier
findings.summary: Embed permanent metadata or another provenance mechanism, as far as technically feasible, including a unique identifier for the service that made the content.
findings.quote: shall be embedded with a permanent metadata or other appropriate technical provenance mechanisms, to the extent technically feasible, including a unique identifier

sources.title: Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Amendment Rules, 2026, notification G.S.R. 120(E) of 10 February 2026, Gazette of India, as published by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology

findings.title: A prominent label on realistic synthetic media
findings.summary: If your service can create realistic AI audio, images or video of people or events that could pass as real, label the output prominently, or for audio with a prefixed audio disclosure. Text and content that is plainly not realistic are outside the definition; routine editing, accessibility and translation are excluded.
findings.quote: prominently labelled in a manner that ensures prominent visibility in the visual display that is easily noticeable and adequately perceivable

sources.title: Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Amendment Rules, 2026, notification G.S.R. 120(E) of 10 February 2026, Gazette of India, as published by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology

findings.title: Stop unlawful synthetic content being made
findings.summary: Take reasonable technical measures, including automated tools, so users cannot create or share unlawful synthetic content: child sexual abuse material, non-consensual intimate imagery, false documents, weapons instructions, or content that falsely depicts a real person or event to deceive.

sources.title: Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Amendment Rules, 2026, notification G.S.R. 120(E) of 10 February 2026, Gazette of India, as published by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology

findings.title: Remind users of the rules every three months
findings.summary: Remind users of your rules at least once every three months, and tell them that misusing synthetic-content tools may lead to penalties, removal, account suspension and, where the law allows, disclosure of their identity to a victim.

sources.title: Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Amendment Rules, 2026, notification G.S.R. 120(E) of 10 February 2026, Gazette of India, as published by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology

answers.question: Do India's AI labelling rules cover AI-generated text?
answers.description: No: India's rules on synthetically generated information cover realistic audio, images and video, not text. What the definition reaches, with sources.
answers.answer: No. India's rules define synthetically generated information as audio, visual or audio-visual content that appears real, so text is outside them, as is content that plainly does not look real.

answers.question: Do New York ads with AI-generated people need a disclosure?
answers.description: Yes, since 9 June 2026: an ad featuring a synthetic performer must say so conspicuously. Who it binds, the exemptions and the penalty, with sources.
answers.answer: Yes, if the person in the ad is AI-generated, looks human and is not an identifiable real person: since 9 June 2026, whoever produces the ad, knowing this, must disclose conspicuously in it that a synthetic performer is in it. Audio ads and translation of a real performer are exempt.

findings.title: Disclose a synthetic performer in your ad
findings.summary: If you produce an advertisement for New York featuring an AI-generated person who looks human but is not an identifiable real person, and you know it, disclose conspicuously in the ad that a synthetic performer is in it. Audio ads, AI used only to translate a human performer, and promotions of expressive works that use the performer the same way are exempt. $1,000 for a first violation, $5,000 after.
findings.quote: shall conspicuously disclose in such advertisement that a synthetic performer is in such advertisement

sources.title: New York General Business Law section 396-b, Advertisements, on the New York State Senate's site
Senate Bill S8420-A (2025), signed 11 December 2025 as Chapter 617 of the Laws of 2025

answers.question: Do I have to label AI-generated videos on TikTok?
answers.description: Yes, if they show realistic scenes or people: TikTok requires creators to label them, and labels content carrying Content Credentials itself.
answers.answer: Yes, if they show realistic-looking scenes or people: TikTok requires creators to label AI-generated or significantly edited content of that kind, and may remove, restrict or label what is not. Content that carries Content Credentials is labelled automatically.

findings.title: TikTok: label realistic AI content when you post it
findings.summary: TikTok requires creators to label AI-generated or significantly edited content that shows realistic-looking scenes or people. Unlabelled content may be removed, restricted or labelled by TikTok.
findings.quote: we require creators to label AI-generated or significantly edited content that shows realistic-looking scenes or people

sources.title: TikTok Community Guidelines, Integrity and Authenticity: Edited Media and AI-Generated Content

findings.title: TikTok labels content that carries Content Credentials
findings.summary: TikTok reads Content Credentials on upload and labels images and videos that carry them as AI-generated automatically.
findings.quote: TikTok is starting to automatically label AI-generated content (AIGC) when it's uploaded from certain other platforms
findings.unverified: What TikTok shows for a signer that is not on the C2PA trust list, and whether marks survive its re-encode, is not stated; we are measuring it.

sources.title: TikTok Newsroom, Partnering with our industry to advance AI transparency and literacy (9 May 2024)

answers.question: Do AI images need a label on Instagram and Facebook?
answers.description: Meta requires labels on photorealistic video and realistic audio, not images, but labels images 'AI Info' when they carry C2PA or IPTC metadata.
answers.answer: Not from you: Meta's labelling duty covers photorealistic video and realistic-sounding audio, not images. Meta labels images "AI Info" itself when it detects industry-standard indicators such as the C2PA and IPTC metadata in a signed manifest.

findings.title: Meta labels marked content "AI Info"
findings.summary: Meta labels images "AI Info" when it detects industry-standard indicators, including the C2PA and IPTC metadata that a signed manifest carries.
findings.quote: These labels are now displayed as 'AI Info'
findings.unverified: Whether the manifest and watermark survive in the file after upload, and what Meta shows for an untrusted signer, are not stated; we are measuring them.

answers.question: Do I have to disclose AI-generated video on YouTube?
answers.description: Yes, for realistic content: YouTube asks creators to disclose it in Studio, and labels uploads carrying C2PA metadata itself. The policy and sources.
answers.answer: Yes, when AI meaningfully alters or generates photorealistic content: YouTube requires you to say so in YouTube Studio's "AI use" question. An upload carrying C2PA metadata is labelled automatically, and you cannot remove that label.

findings.title: YouTube: disclose realistic AI content in the upload flow
findings.summary: YouTube requires creators to disclose when AI meaningfully alters or generates photorealistic content, by answering the "AI use" question in YouTube Studio. Disclosing does not limit reach or earnings; repeatedly not disclosing can lead to a label, removal or Partner Program suspension.
findings.quote: we require creators to disclose when they use AI to meaningfully alter or generate photorealistic content

sources.title: YouTube Help, Disclosing use of altered or synthetic content

findings.title: YouTube labels uploads that carry C2PA metadata
findings.summary: YouTube may label content containing C2PA metadata automatically, and a creator cannot remove a label that C2PA metadata triggered.
findings.quote: content made with YouTube's AI tools, content with C2PA metadata, or content labeled after manual review cannot be adjusted

sources.title: YouTube Help, Disclosing use of altered or synthetic content

answers.question: Does LinkedIn show who made an AI image?
answers.description: Yes: LinkedIn shows a C2PA icon on images and video with Content Credentials, and the panel names the issuer, whoever signed the manifest.
answers.answer: It shows who signed it. Images and video with Content Credentials get a C2PA icon on LinkedIn, and the panel behind it shows whether AI was used, the app, the creator, the issuer and the date. The issuer is whoever signed the manifest: your supplier, unless you sign under your own name.

findings.title: LinkedIn shows Content Credentials, including who issued them
findings.summary: Images and videos with Content Credentials get a C2PA icon on LinkedIn; clicking it shows whether AI was used, the app or device, the creator, the issuer and the date. The issuer is whoever signed the manifest.
findings.quote: The icon will be visible to all viewers of your content.
findings.unverified: Which trust list LinkedIn checks, and what it shows for a signer that is not on the C2PA trust list, are not stated.

sources.title: LinkedIn Help, Content Credentials
